target_customer: Insurance agents, carriers, mortgage companies and asset managers who want to know when hail hits a specific property
problem: After severe hail, hidden roof damage often goes unclaimed or is found late. Insurers and property owners lack property-level, near real time hail exposure data.
business_model: B2B and B2B2C SaaS subscription per monitored address
product_category: Insurtech weather and property hail monitoring

founders.name: Demetrius Gray
prior_employers: Storm roofing contractor business he owned (described by the YC blog as the largest minority-owned roofing company in the U.S.)
founders.background_notes: Hypepotamus (2018-10) says he spent a decade as a storm roofing contractor.

founders.name: Jermaine Watkins
founders.background_notes: YC page bio claims 20+ years building web and e-commerce applications.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed to ingest and compute geo-weather data at property level and alert quickly. The company later relied on a third party weather API (Xweather) rather than building its own weather data, so the hard part was product and data pipelines, not meteorology research.

defensibility.rationale: Weather data is available from several vendors and alerts are easy to copy. Insurer relationships and a database of monitored structures (30,000 rooftops in Oct 2018, 2.7 million structures per the YC launch post) gave some stickiness.

incumbents: Weather data vendors and catastrophe analytics firms
takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found showing an incumbent copying or buying WeatherCheck. The company won an InsureTech Connect innovation prize in 2019-09.

market_need_then: Hail is a large source of insured property loss, and the founder saw as a roofing contractor that clients often did not file claims after storms. Insurers and mortgage lenders wanted faster exposure insight.

branding.brand_signature: First Kentucky company in Y Combinator, per press coverage
branding.community_and_virality: Local press and podcast coverage in Louisville about the YC acceptance; no evidence of merch or fan community.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name that fits the product but is generic and shared with other weather products. Press focused on the YC milestone, not on the brand.

outcome_analysis: WeatherCheck was founded by a roofing contractor and a developer, entered YC in Winter 2019 as the first Kentucky company, and won an InsureTech Connect innovation challenge in 2019-09. The company was still listed as Active with about 10 people. No verified funding rounds or exit were found, so its financial trajectory beyond the YC stage is unknown. The CEO later founded another company, so the story may not be a simple continuation.
notes: The company website field is blank in the directory; no site was fetched, the YC page links only social profiles and a GitHub org. Funding is unverified: Hypepotamus (2018-10-16) says the team was raising a $5.5M Series A, with no confirmation that it closed. Aggregators (Seedtable, Village.ai) list a roughly $150K seed in 2019-03 and totals around $215K, which conflict with each other and are not recorded as rounds. Competitors: search for 2019 era hail alert vendors returned only undated directory pages (Hailios, HailStrike and others), so the list is empty rather than padded. A later article says the CEO went on to found Captain; no source found for the fate of WeatherCheck itself. Completeness pass 2026-11: a $150K seed (2019-03) is now recorded from Seedtable; Geek Estate Blog also says $150K from 2 investors, but there is no press release. Seedtable's investor split is an estimate, so investors are left empty. Femtech Health lists $215K total (pre-seed 2020-03) and ZoomInfo $64K debt in 2021, unreconciled, so coverage is partial. Captain's later $100M debt and $7.3M equity belong to a different company.
